discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Cirac turned Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a concrete, realizable program. Their 1998 proposal (with Jaksch, Bruder and Gardiner) showed that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model, with tunable interactions and a superfluid to Mott-insulator transition. Bloch's 2002 experiment observed that transition, and his group went on to pioneer quantum gas microscopy, measurements of entanglement and many-body localization, and studies of out-of-equilibrium dynamics. Together, this theory-experiment partnership created a new field in which strongly correlated condensed-matter models, artificial gauge fields, topological phases and lattice gauge theories are engineered and probed atom by atom. The ideas now underpin analog and digital quantum simulators worldwide, including Rydberg-atom and tweezer-array platforms. It is a rare example of a simple, usable theoretical framework that experimentalists adopted directly and that unified quantum optics, condensed matter and quantum information.
